title: Social Psychology: Definition, Nature & Scope
summary: Social psychology defined as the scientific study of how individuals' thoughts, feelings and behaviours are influenced by the actual, imagined or implied presence of others. Covers nature, scope, levels of analysis and relation to other social sciences.
objectives: Describe the nature and scope of social psychology.
Identify the three levels of analysis.
revision: Social psychology: definition, nature, scope and levels of analysis (intrapersonal, interpersonal, intergroup).
traps: Social psychology = scientific study of individual in social context.

notes.t: The scientific study of how individuals think, feel and behave in social situations, and how the actual, imagined or implied presence of others influences behaviour.
Social psychology bridges psychology and sociology, focusing on the individual within the social context rather than on society as a whole.

i: Scientific method: observation, hypothesis testing, experimentation
Focus on the individual in the social situation
Study of social influence, social cognition and social behaviour
Applied to real-world issues: prejudice, aggression, helping, groups
Intergroup: prejudice, group dynamics, social identity

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks for the definition of social psychology and its distinction from sociology and personality psychology.

mnemonics.title: STIF
mnemonics.text: S — Scientific study, T — Thoughts feelings behaviour, I — Implied/actual/imagined presence, F — Focus on individual in context

flashcards.a: Scientific study of how individuals think, feel and behave in social situations.
